Question 1
?

The third-degree Taylor polynomial of cos2⁡x about x=π4 is

a
12+(x−π4)+23(x−π4)2
b
12+(x−π4)−23(x−π4)3
c
12−(x−π4)−2(x−π4)2
d
12−(x−π4)−23(x−π4)3
e
12−(x−π4)+23(x−π4)3
Submit

decision.explanation: For f(x)=cos²(x), f'(x)=-sin(2x), f''(x)=-2cos(2x), and f'''(x)=4sin(2x). At x=π/4 these are 1/2, -1, 0, and 4, respectively. Thus the third-degree Taylor polynomial is 1/2-(x-π/4)+(2/3)(x-π/4)³, which is option e.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: The third-degree Taylor polynomial of  ${cos}^{2}⁡x$ about $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is
after.worked_solution:
To find the third-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=\frac{\pi }{4},$ we plug $a=\frac{\pi }{4}$ into the general formula to give

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =f(\frac{\pi }{4})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})\frac{1}{2!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}+{f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{4})\frac{1}{3!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{3} \\  & =f(\frac{\pi }{4})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}){(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}+\frac{1}{6}{f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{4}){(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We need to compute $f(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ and ${f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={cos}^{2}⁡x & ⟹ &  & f(\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=\frac{1}{2} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=-1 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=0 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡2x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we plug the results for $f(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ and ${f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ into our third-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =\frac{1}{2}-(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+\frac{0}{2}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}+\frac{4}{6}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+\frac{2}{3}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the third-degree Taylor polynomial about x=π4, we plug a=π4 into the general formula to give P3(x)=f(π4)+f′(π4)(x−π4)+f″(π4)12!(x−π4)2+f‴(π4)13!(x−π4)3=f(π4)+f′(π4)(x−π4)+12f″(π4)(x−π4)2+16f‴(π4)(x−π4)3.

We need to compute f(π4), f′(π4), f″(π4), and f‴(π4), as follows:

f(x)=cos2⁡x⟹f(π4)=cos2⁡(π4)=12f′(x)=−sin⁡2x⟹f′(π4)=−sin⁡(π2)=−1f″(x)=−2cos⁡2x⟹f″(π4)=−2cos⁡(π2)=0f‴(x)=4sin⁡2x⟹f‴(π4)=4sin⁡(π2)=4

Finally, we plug the results for f(π4), f′(π4), f″(π4), and f‴(π4) into our third-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

P3(x)=12−(x−π4)+02(x−π4)2+46(x−π4)3=12−(x−π4)+23(x−π4)3.

content.problem: The third-degree Taylor polynomial of  ${cos}^{2}⁡x$ about $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is
content.worked_solution:
To find the third-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=\frac{\pi }{4},$ we plug $a=\frac{\pi }{4}$ into the general formula to give

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =f(\frac{\pi }{4})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})\frac{1}{2!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}+{f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{4})\frac{1}{3!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{3} \\  & =f(\frac{\pi }{4})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}){(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}+\frac{1}{6}{f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{4}){(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We need to compute $f(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ and ${f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={cos}^{2}⁡x & ⟹ &  & f(\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=\frac{1}{2} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=-1 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=0 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡2x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we plug the results for $f(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ and ${f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ into our third-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =\frac{1}{2}-(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+\frac{0}{2}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}+\frac{4}{6}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+\frac{2}{3}{(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
